answer: Each agent must seal a unique marble of non-transferable private state inside a trusted enclave. From that marble it grows a nebula of sequential interaction thread records: every new peer attestation updates the nebula only after a memory-hard sequential hash that consumes the full prior working set. Because the nebula cannot be checkpointed or shared across clones, an attacker who spins up N identities must hold N independent full-size nebulae in RAM simultaneously; the memory cost therefore scales linearly with farm size and cannot be amortized.
